findings.message: main() catches only BrokenPipeError, but this silencing is incomplete: on Windows a write to a closed downstream pipe surfaces as OSError with errno EINVAL (not BrokenPipeError), so `dupefinder ... | head` still prints a traceback on Windows despite the cross-platform contract, and on any platform buffered stdout is flushed at interpreter shutdown, which can still hit the broken pipe and emit 'Exc

_is_special issues up to four separate stat() calls per candidate (is_fifo/is_socket/is_block_device/is_char_device each stat independently), and _walk calls it for every entry on top of the path.is_symlink() stat, so directory enumeration pays up to five stats per file. For a duplicate scanner whose whole job is walking large trees this is a measurable slowdown; one lstat plus a single stat.S_IFM

_silence_pipe leaves the devnull descriptor from os.open open after os.dup2; it is a one-shot per process so the impact is tiny, but closing it is free and keeps the helper leak-free if it is ever called more than once in embedded runs.
findings.patch_new:
devnull_fd = os.open(os.devnull, os.O_WRONLY)
    try:
        os.dup2(devnull_fd, stdout_fd)
    finally:
        os.close(devnull_fd)
